primitives.name: Spatial Postprocessing Adaptation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Research question How do statistical (EMOS-R/C/L, boosted EMOS) vs ML (DRN, GraphSAGE GNN, Transformer) post-processing methods for ECMWF 2-m temperature and 10-m wind speed compare at observed vs unobserved stations, and can an altitude-aware linear pool (ALP) improve forecast combination at unobserved locations?
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: CRPSS (skill score, dimensionless); RMSES (root-mean-square error, K); coverage (dimensionless); RI (reliability index, dimensionless)
primitives.assumptions: Exchangeable ensemble members; Gaussian/TN predictive distributions; station assignments via Euclidean feature distance; rolling windows capture non-stationarity
primitives.breakdown_regime: Observed stations → perfect calibration; unobserved stations → catastrophic overdispersion

layer2.mapping: GSI → conformal prediction via split-sample calibration; GSE → situational reasoning via regional/spectral state transitions

primitives.name: Altitudinal Linear Pooling
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Standard linear pool (SLP): F^(w) = wΦ((y-μ1)/σ1) + (1-w)Φ((y-μ2)/σ2), w estimated by minimum-CRPS on a 60-day rolling window; ALP: separate w per altitude group (<300 m, 300–700 m, ≥700 m), each unobserved station gets its group's weight.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: w (weight, dimensionless); Φ (Gaussian CDF); CRPS (continuous ranked probability score, K)
primitives.assumptions: Linear combination preserves proper calibration; altitude groups are exchangeable within bands; optimal weights are constant over rolling windows

layer2.mapping: GSI → hierarchical Bayes with random effects; GSE → multi-armed bandit allocation for venue-type pools
layer2.telemetry: Weight stability, interval coverage, CRPSS improvement

primitives.name: Transformer Attention
primitives.verbatim_quote: - DRN (MLP), GraphSAGE GNN (Haversine ≤ 50 km edges, mean aggregation, fixed graph), Transformer (self-attention across stations, no fixed graph) — all output Gaussian/TN parameters by minimizing closed-form CRPS; 10 replications each.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Self-attention matrix A ∈ ℝ^{N×N} (adjacency, dimensionless); N (number of stations)
primitives.assumptions: Station relationships are learned from data; attention heads capture non-Euclidean dependencies; model is invariant to station ordering
primitives.breakdown_regime: Long-range dependencies → sparse, inefficient graphs; small sample sizes → overfitting

layer2.mapping: GSI → kernel regression with learned similarity metrics; GSE → dynamic routing via attention-based state transitions

primitives.name: Semi-Local Clustering
primitives.verbatim_quote: 1), minimum-CRPS; semi-local = k-means on climatology + error features (8–10 clusters).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: k-means cluster centroids μ_k (K); cluster assignments z_i (integer)
primitives.assumptions: Climatology and error variance explain most heteroscedasticity; clusters are compact and separable; optimal k is known
primitives.breakdown_regime: Outlying stations → mis-assigned clusters, poor local fit

layer2.mapping: GSI → nearest-neighbour conformal; GSE → contextual bandits with regional affinity kernels

reasoning_traces.think:
The core failure mode is 'overfitting-to-observation': traditional EMOS models excel at fitting the exact stations used during training, but they completely ignore the spatial correlation structure that exists between nearby stations. This leads to perfect calibration at observed stations and catastrophic under-dispersion at unobserved ones. The study demonstrates that ML methods (especially DRN and Transformers) and semi-local clustering explicitly model this spatial correlation, yielding much better out-of-sample performance. Altitudinal linear pooling then provides a robust way to combine multiple imperfect models, particularly for extreme elevations where individual model confidence drops.
